ext.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) for VS Code: renders the DSH Web GUI faithfully in a sidebar or editor tab with auto-detection and auto-start, without touching how you reorganize DSH itself or assemble third-party plugins; since v0.7.13 it also registers DSH as a Copilot chat model — a DeepSeek Harness entry appears in the model picker, takes the conversations Copilot has prepared, strips prompts unrelated to the chat content, hands them to DSH for re-organization and streams the answer back, putting DSH's task orchestration and tool-calling to full use; it detects the official Windows desktop build and starts it with its built-in dsh CLI (no npm/Node needed), custom install directories (like E:\DSH) included; in Remote-WSL / Remote-SSH panels you can sign in to your DeepSeek account using the local browser; the in-panel copy button works through the host clipboard relay; companion plugins are written to two locations so pnpm cannot silently clean them, and file links also take over local <a href> paths

cfg.dshPanel.locale.desc: Display language for this extension's own UI text (auto follows the VS Code display language; zh/en forces a single language). It does not change the DSH page itself. Note: command menus and settings descriptions come from the extension manifest and follow the VS Code display language, so this setting does not change them (the extension warns once when the two differ)
cfg.dshPanel.locale.enum.auto: Follow the VS Code display language
cfg.dshPanel.url.desc: Address of the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI (local, or forwarded through an SSH tunnel)
cfg.dshPanel.host.desc: Host address to bind when auto-starting dsh
cfg.dshPanel.port.desc: Port to listen on when auto-starting dsh
cfg.dshPanel.autoStart.desc: Whether to run dsh web automatically when DSH is detected as not running
cfg.dshPanel.autoRegisterWorkspace.desc: Register the current VS Code workspace in DSH's workspace list (idempotent). It only registers — it does not change DSH's currently selected workspace (that is dshPanel.pinWorkspaceToVSCode's job)
cfg.dshPanel.pinWorkspaceToVSCode.desc: When the panel opens, switch DSH's current workspace to the folder VS Code has open (installs the companion plugin dsh-vscode-workspace automatically). No-op when already in that workspace; when off: no plugin install, no switch, no path sent
cfg.dshPanel.openSystemBrowser.desc: Keep the old pop-the-system-browser behavior when the extension starts dsh web (off by default: the new dsh web completes browser sign-in automatically, ready right in the panel)
cfg.dshPanel.installClipboardPlugin.desc: Automatically install the bundled dsh-webview-clipboard plugin (since v0.3.0: on every platform it relays in-panel navigator.clipboard.writeText through the host into the clipboard, fixing copy buttons that silently fail; it also fixes macOS in-panel copy/paste and other editing shortcuts). If you suspect it interferes with dsh web startup, turn it off and compare
cfg.dshPanel.installOpenExternalPlugin.d: Automatically install the bundled dsh-vscode-open-external plugin (since v1.1.0): takes over window.open in the DSH page (typical case: the DeepSeek account authorization page) and <a> new window/new tab clicks; window.open opens in the system browser — under Remote-SSH / Remote-WSL the client browser (e.g. Windows) opens it, solving sign-in when the remote side has no graphical browser. Where <a> clicks actually go is decided by dshPanel.externalLinkAction
cfg.dshPanel.externalLinkAction.mdesc: How an external http(s) link opens when clicked inside the panel: a plain click on `<a target="_blank">`, a Ctrl/Cmd/Shift click, or a middle click. Clicks DSH handles itself (for example a chat link's "open in sidebar") are unaffected; `target="_self"` and sign-in authorization pages keep the original DSH/system browser behavior. `off` only turns off this click bridge — it does not affect the `window.open` sign-in path.
cfg.dshPanel.externalLinkAction.enum.off: Do not take over <a> new window/new tab clicks (keeps DSH's current behavior; window.open login/new tab links still open as before)
cfg.dshPanel.externalLinkAction.enum.sys: Open in the system default browser (under Remote-SSH / Remote-WSL the client browser opens it)
cfg.dshPanel.externalLinkAction.enum.vsc: Open in a new tab with VS Code's built-in browser (Simple Browser / browser view)
cfg.dshPanel.forwardVSCodeKeys.desc: Whether to forward VS Code keybindings while the panel has focus (installs the companion plugin dsh-vscode-keys automatically). Before forwarding it checks DSH's own key table and yields on a hit, so DSH's shortcuts are never stolen. When off, behavior is exactly as if the feature did not exist (no plugin installed, no keys listened to).
cfg.dshPanel.forwardKeybindings.mdesc:
Add or remove keys on top of the default forward table: a command id as the value forwards to that command, `false` never intercepts.

Key names must be "modifier + primary key": `mod` (⌘ on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere), `ctrl`, `meta`, `alt`, `shift`; the primary key may be a letter, digit, `f1`–`f24` or a code name (like `backquote`, `comma`).

Chords (like `ctrl+k ctrl+s`) are not supported; unmodified single keys are never intercepted either (that would break the input box).

Example: `{ "ctrl+shift+y": "workbench.action.togglePanel", "ctrl+shift+f": false }`
cfg.dshPanel.focusReleaseKey.mdesc: The key that hands focus back to VS Code from inside the panel (default `F6`). Pressing it moves focus off the DSH page, after which any custom keys and chords work; click the panel to go back to DSH. Set an empty string to disable this behavior (key forwarding is unaffected).
cfg.dshPanel.focusInputEnabled.mdesc:
Whether to provide the default shortcut `Ctrl+Shift+J` (`⇧⌘J` on macOS) for "Focus DSH Input". When off, that combination never takes effect and never occupies your keys; the command still works from the Command Palette. To use a different combination, search `dshPanel.focusInput` in Keyboard Shortcuts and edit it (the extension cannot register keys dynamically).

Note: combinations with `Alt` are treated as AltGr character input in the terminal (bottom panel) and may not come out; if a custom combination also stops responding in the bottom panel, add the command to `terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell`.
cfg.dshPanel.workspaceFileLinkAction.des: Click behavior for workspace file/folder links in DSH chats (implemented by auto-installing the companion plugin dsh-vscode-file-links). It only takes over when the target is inside the current VS Code workspace and really exists; otherwise the DSH sidebar keeps opening it. Ctrl/Cmd/Shift/Alt click temporarily uses the DSH sidebar
cfg.dshPanel.workspaceFileLinkAction.enu: When a workspace file/folder link in a DSH chat is clicked, reveal and open it in the VS Code Explorer (files open the editor, folders are only revealed)

Reveal + show the changes: prefer opening "this turn's changes" side by side (left/right are the original text at the turn's start/end, titled like a.ts · Turn 7); when unavailable, fall back to "diff against HEAD", and if that fails open the original file; installs the companion plugin dsh-vscode-changes. If the target is outside the current VS Code workspace (or deleted this turn), only DSH's own turn records produce the diff — no disk reads, no Explorer reveal
Only reveal and select in this window's VS Code Explorer, without opening an editor
Do not take over: keep DSH's own behavior (opens in the DSH sidebar). The companion plugin dsh-vscode-file-links is not installed either
cfg.dshPanel.outOfWorkspaceFileAccess.md:
Whether to hand files **outside the workspace** to VS Code (default `false`: keep opening in the DSH sidebar).

Why it is off by default: paths in links come from the model, and passing them straight to VS Code (`stat` / open / diff against git) turns **any** path outside the workspace into a reachable one. DSH's turn-level change records live only in process memory, so **after a dsh web restart old turns have no data** — out-of-workspace files then have no viewable source at all, and only the DSH sidebar remains.

When on: `diffAndOpen` tries the turn records first, then falls back to "diff of the file against git `HEAD`", then opens the out-of-workspace file directly; `revealAndOpen` / `revealOnly` open/reveal that file directly.
cfg.dshPanel.dshSidebar.desc: DSH sidebar display policy. Hiding is done by cropping the parent container's viewport (no injection, no rewriting of the DSH page) and can be toggled anytime from the top toolbar; a manual toggle takes precedence over this setting, and changing this setting clears the manual toggle
cfg.dshPanel.dshSidebar.enum.auto: Hide the DSH sidebar in narrow panels (under 1024px, such as the sidebar or bottom panel) and keep it visible in wide panels (such as editor tabs)
cfg.dshPanel.dshSidebar.enum.show: Always show the DSH sidebar (same as turning this feature off: no cropping, no measurement plugin installed)
cfg.dshPanel.debugLogToFile.desc: Write the debug log to a file (off by default). When on, sidebar crop diagnostics (page-side + panel-side timelines), manual show/hide, policy changes, plugin install changes and similar events are appended under this extension's global storage: <globalStorage>/logs/dsh-vscode-debug.log (that is globalStorage/<extension id>/logs/ inside the VS Code user data directory; historical logs from ~/.dsh-debug are copied over once when upgrading from an older version). Past 2MB it auto-rotates to .log.1 (one copy kept). The log holds only layout numbers and short enums, sanitized before writing (no tokens or conversation content). When investigating, pair it with the command "DeepSeek Harness: Open Debug Log"
cfg.dshPanel.autoInstallDsh.desc: Whether to prompt and install on your behalf when dsh is not installed in the current environment (including remote servers) (npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh). Note: the official Windows desktop build is detected automatically and never reaches this path
cfg.dshPanel.dshCommand.desc: The dsh command (resolved from PATH by default; when not found it automatically tries the official Windows desktop build's bundled CLI and npx. To force a full path, e.g. C:\Users\you\AppData\Roaming\npm\dsh.cmd or <desktop install dir>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd)
cfg.dshPanel.remoteAuthProxy.desc: Whether to enable the managed auth proxy in truly remote windows (Remote-SSH / Dev Containers etc., on by default): the extension runs a proxy on the server's loopback interface and hands it to the webview through port forwarding, so the panel and the Copilot bridge work without signing in. The proxy listens on the server loopback only, but other users on the same machine who enumerate that port can reach your DSH through it (bypassing the startup token). On a multi-user shared server it is recommended to turn this off; the panel then shows browser sign-in guidance
cfg.dshPanel.killOnDispose.desc: Whether to end dsh processes started by this extension when it deactivates or VS Code closes (does not touch dsh you started yourself)
cfg.dshPanel.chatAgentPreset.desc: Agent preset used when DSH model sessions are created (like liangshen); leave empty for the default preset from DSH settings
cfg.dshPanel.chatProvider.desc: Model provider used by the DSH (DeepSeek Harness) model entry (provider id, must already be configured in DSH settings, like deepseek-official); leave empty to follow the DSH default model
cfg.dshPanel.chatModel.desc: Model id used by the DSH (DeepSeek Harness) model entry (together with chatProvider, like deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-pro); leave empty to follow the DSH default model
cfg.dshPanel.chatTimeoutMs.desc: Maximum wait for a single task (milliseconds); on timeout the task keeps running in the DSH panel
cfg.dshPanel.chatSyncLookbackMin.desc: How many minutes of recently modified chat session files to scan when locating the current Copilot chat
cfg.dshPanel.enableDshModel.desc: Register DSH as a VS Code chat model (a DSH (DeepSeek Harness) entry appears in the model picker); pick it and DSH solves the task
cfg.dshPanel.debugModelMessages.desc: Debug: write the structure of messages VS Code sends to the DSH model into the workspace .dsh-debug/ directory
cfg.dshPanel.markForeignAssistant.desc: When switching back to the DSH model to replay the middle of a conversation, whether to tag answers produced by other models with a provenance marker (helps DSH tell which answers it did not generate itself); turn off to skip tagging
cfg.dshPanel.dshReasoningEffort.desc: Fallback reasoning effort for the DSH model (reasoningEffort): off/low/high/max; a choice in the chat UI wins and this setting only applies when the UI has none; leave empty to follow the DSH default level
